name: Electric Power-Assisted Bicycle
description: A vehicle on no more than three wheels with pedals, a seat and an electric motor with an input of no more than 750 watts, in one of three classes: pedal-assist to 20 mph, throttle-capable to 20 mph, or pedal-assist to 28 mph. Defined by Code of Virginia §46.2-100 and regulated by §46.2-904.1.

restrictions.rule: Class one assists only while pedaling and stops at 20 mph; class two can propel the bike on its own and stops assisting at 20 mph; class three assists only while pedaling and stops at 28 mph
No more than three wheels, pedals for human propulsion, a seat, and a motor with an input of no more than 750 watts
The motor disengages or stops when the rider stops pedaling or applies the brakes
Meets the CPSC's bicycle requirements (16 CFR part 1512), and a class three must have a speedometer showing its speed in miles per hour
Manufacturers and distributors must permanently affix a label in at least 9-point Arial stating its class, top assisted speed and motor wattage
Must not be tampered with or modified to change its motor-powered speed or engagement unless the label is replaced to match
Batteries must be spill-proof, sealed or gelled-electrolyte
Riders under 14 may ride a class three only under the immediate supervision of someone 18 or older
Every rider and passenger on a class three must wear a bicycle helmet meeting CPSC or ASTM standards; a locality may require helmets for riders 14 and under on any class
Ridden wherever bicycles are allowed, including streets, highways, shoulders, bike lanes and bicycle or shared-use paths, but never on an Interstate highway

A locality or state agency may ban class one or two from a bicycle or shared-use path only after notice and a public hearing, for safety or legal reasons, and may ban class three from one without a hearing
On a natural-surface trail designated nonmotorized, the locality or agency that manages it may regulate e-bike use
Allowed on sidewalks unless a locality bans it there by ordinance or signs prohibit it; on a sidewalk or shared-use path the rider must yield to pedestrians and give an audible signal before passing
Has a bicycle's rights and duties: no driver's license, registration, title, license plate or insurance
